caveats: Distance is in a straight line. Roads, rivers, hills and public transport can make a short distance a long journey.

Distance is measured from the centre of each local authority, not from where each person lives. In a large local authority many people are much nearer or much farther than the figure says, and a site can be inside the place and still be far from its centre.
The figures say how far people are from a site. They do not say how far the people you see travel, or whether anyone far away needs you.
The residents are everyone counted on census day, 21 March 2021, of every age. Not all of them need what you offer.

# Version 0.1 of this analysis, run with
# uk-open-data 0.2.0a1. This runs it again with
# the same settings. No row or heading of your table is written
# here: put the name of your own column beside each role.
import pandas as pd

from uk_open_data.analyses import run_analysis

data = pd.read_csv("your-table.csv")
result = run_analysis(
    "access-distance",
    data,
    columns={
        "latitude": "",  # the name of your column
        "longitude": "",  # the name of your column
    },
    options={
        "postcode_lookup": "auto",
        "need": "residents",
        "catchment": ["Newcastle upon Tyne", "North Tyneside", "South Tyneside", "Gateshead", "Sunderland", "Northumberland", "County Durham"],
        "within_km": 10,
        "top": 10,
    },
)
print(result.answer)
for figure in result.figures:
    print(figure.label, figure.value)
